I farm in Quzhou County, so I will keep the system simple, intensive, and low-risk. I will base the year on the wheat-maize rotation because it fits my climate, my irrigation conditions, and the way I want to use land efficiently across the full year. At the start of this season, my winter wheat is already the main crop on the land, so I will manage that carefully through jointing, booting, and grain filling, with moderate fertilizer, a few irrigations, and tight disease control. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize so I do not lose heat or moisture, and I will use improved or hybrid seed to stabilize yield. Because I am educated and I care about efficiency, I will avoid overly traditional low-input management; I will use measured fertilizer, timely irrigation, and targeted pesticide applications rather than either neglect or excessive spraying. I will mostly use rotary tillage for convenience and speed between crops, and I will keep input levels high enough to protect yield but not so high that I waste money or increase lodging and pest pressure.
